name: Vatnajökull National Park
blurb: Ice cap, outwash plains and a glacial lagoon where seals, terns and skuas hunt.

tip.title: Remove the herring
tip.text: Tides bring herring into the glacial lagoon. Set Atlantic herring to -100% and watch seals, terns and skuas, and the Arctic fox that preys on tern.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Silty rivers and lakes fed by melting ice shape the lowlands, lay down outwash sands and feed the lagoon at the glacier edge.

nodes.name: Soil microbes and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, droppings and carcasses, returning nutrients to the thin soil.
A low evergreen heath shrub with black berries, widespread on Icelandic moors and eaten by reindeer, ptarmigan and snow buntings.
A dwarf heath shrub whose leaves and berries are food for reindeer, ptarmigan and small birds.
A small tundra flower with edible leaves and bulbils, eaten by geese and ptarmigan.
Drifting microscopic algae in the sea and glacial lagoon that feed small crustaceans and fish. General ecological knowledge.

nodes.name: Reindeer
nodes.desc: Introduced to Iceland in the 18th century, the East Iceland herd grazes heath and highland plants, with lichen a winter staple.
A hardy grouse that stays all year and eats shoots, buds, leaves and berries of heath plants.

nodes.name: Snow bunting
nodes.desc: A small songbird of rocky highlands and shores that eats seeds and berries of heath plants.

nodes.name: Non-biting midges
nodes.desc: Their larvae live in lake and river mud on algae and detritus, and are food for fish. General ecological knowledge.
Tides carry herring from the sea into Jökulsárlón, where seals, terns and skuas feed on them.
A cold-water fish of Icelandic lakes and rivers that feeds largely on insect larvae and other small invertebrates.
A clever omnivore and scavenger that takes carrion as well as berries and other plant food.

nodes.name: Harbour seal
nodes.desc: Gathers at the mouth of Jökulsárlón, especially in winter, to hunt fish brought in by the tide.
Iceland's only native land mammal, a mostly bird-eating predator that also scavenges carcasses.

story: Vatnajökull National Park in Iceland covers 14,967 km2, making it Europe's second largest national park. Established on June 7, 2008, and inscribed as a World Heritage Site on July 5, 2019, it encompasses the vast Vatnajökull glacier and features a landscape shaped by rivers, glacial ice, and volcanic and geothermal activity.
matters: Areas near the glacier and around Snæfell provide an important habitat for reindeer and pink-footed geese. The park aims to preserve unimpaired natural beauty for future generations.
